_extraction_note: extraction-by-restoration works for the late-stack capitalization ensemble (2.9x, S1503) but FAILS for mid-stack punctuation circuits (negative class recovery, S1512) — input paths required; S1514: mid-stack heads work when layers 0-6 attention is exact, but that is non-selective — minimal input-path search open; S1516: inputs form in layers 0-3 (early>late 3/3) but whole-layer restoration is a shared trunk — sub-layer feeder search open
_method_note: complementary discovery: cosine-normalized target attribution (output-defined circuits) + attention-to-source patterns (attention-defined); sink confound closed S1524. Selectivity > 50x requires NR=1920 verification (S1523).
_movers_note: heads {5.5, 10.8} are the shared context-matching movers of induction and content-copying (S1521-22)
_unification_note: S1527 CONFIRMED: the 13-head L13-17 committee is the late-stack COPYING apparatus (damage 4.8x concentrated on copied targets; copies non-names too). S1546: the committee is the general proper-name prediction apparatus — copying dominant, novel-name channel via 13.0/13.5.

leg3_unit_truncation_preservation.verdict: top-K unit compression is circuit-safe; caveat: frequency-flavored class rises inflate under truncation

_mlp_unit_membership.finding: CERTIFIED MLP-unit circuit component: 16 hidden units of mlp11 (0.35% of layer) carry a .091 question-mark CE effect at 182.6x selectivity, NR=1920, replicated on a disjoint corpus slice to 0.2%. Pronouns@mlp17 is the diffuse contrast case (K16 only 30% of K64; 4.3x). Weight-side unit ranking fails (signed units); only data-driven class-conditional scoring works.
_mlp_unit_membership.implication: circuits are predominantly attention-head objects (head rises .1-2.1 vs unit rises <=.09) but sub-MLP membership is real and sharply selective for some classes
_mlp_unit_membership.eigen_slice_update: 2026-08-26 CERTIFIED: question@mlp11 component = rank-2 eigen slice of the class-projected quadratic form — class rise .180 at global rise -.0002 (zero cost), NR=1920, held-out slice within 4%. Cleanest single circuit component at any grain. NOT universal (S1574): late-layer (mlp17) spectra are sign-interleaved — slices mix gate and payload, units win at diffuse same-sign sites (is/months). Signed-part split + joint head+slice circuit tests queued. Ledger S1570-S1574.
_mlp_unit_membership.signed_slice_and_joint: 2026-08-26: (1) signed split S=S+−S− resolves mlp17 into per-class (payload, gate) eigen-pairs — pronouns payload +.12 at zero cost inside a −.29 gate; is pure payload .30; rank-8 suffices; signed slices beat units at 2/4 late sites (S1575). (2) FIRST cross-module-type circuit: question = 5 heads {10.5,12.6,15.6,15.1,9.7} + rank-2 mlp11 slice, 99.4% additive, slice marginal .166 at zero added global cost (S1576). Circuits extend beyond attention at the canonical slice grain.

joint_circuits.note: question/pronouns ~100% additive; is/months 84% (a ~16% head<->slice overlap at the late site; leave-one-out attribution in flight). Gates fully class-private at output AND computation level (S1577/S1579); single z-direction mean-substitution is the strongest gate handle (the@mlp17: one direction = -.174, 2x the output-side r8 correction).

_mlp_unit_membership.gate_naming: 2026-08-26: the mlp17 gates are NAMED axes - the-gate IS the determiner-prediction axis (token [ the] rank #1 of 50257 by unembedding alignment; class effect 1.57 std; AUC .922): self-inhibition on the class own axis. pronouns-gate = the she<->he gender contrast axis. REVISION (S1585): the serial-routing claim for the is-circuit was refuted at z-level (payload elevation drops only 16% under head substitution) - model = parallel pathways + CE saturation. Gate function (S1586): blunt precision damper - removal damage 44x concentrated at almost-the positions; suppresses true (+22%) and false (+33%) positives alike. S1583-S1586.
_mlp_unit_membership.gender_committee: 2026-08-26: the signed gender readout at mlp17 is a 64-unit committee (1.4% of the layer) reproducing 101% of the .49-CE reflection effect; axis-specific (random-direction control .013). Reflected he-state hedges to NEUTRAL referents (the/they/it), not she - asymmetric gender coding. S1589/S1590. Extraction-property tests for the question and pronoun circuits in flight.

_extraction_asymmetry.finding: removal-certified 5-head circuits recover only .159 (question) / .230 (pronouns) of their class attention gap when all other heads are optimal-constant substituted (MLPs intact); selective (3-6x over global recovery) and 3-4x over random-5 controls. Removal certifies announcers; extraction requires the distributed context assembly. Gender readout depth-localized to mlp17 (20:1 vs mlp13-16).
_extraction_asymmetry.implication: extraction difficulty is the correct price signal for compression-helps-circuits; extraction-vs-K curve and compressed-background extraction in flight
_extraction_asymmetry.resolution: 2026-08-26: extraction against a DEAD (optimal-constant) background is structurally capped and non-monotone (.16/.32/.23/.40 at K=5/10/20/40 — S1334 inversion: mid-rank heads harmful without context). COMPRESSION IS EXTRACTION: the rank-32 whitened-QK background alone preserves 97% of question class function (rise .19 vs 6.0 under constants) and exact circuit heads add nothing (-.08 marginal). A compression class-CE preservation number IS its extraction score. S1593/S1594; rank sweep + pronouns confirmation in flight.

pronouns_compressed_background.finding: compression-is-extraction confirmed on pronouns; exact circuit heads inside the compressed background are ANTI-extraction (mixed-fidelity patching breaks the self-consistent compressed pattern field)

rank_sweep.finding: no knee; class rise halves per rank doubling and tracks global at every rank — compression damage is non-selective, circuit breaks when the model breaks

signed_budget.finding: the '?' channel is a near-cancellation of two large opposing flows: mlp11 (+1028, the module that also READS the channel) against mlp17 (-1151, the largest single contribution in the whole budget, and suppressive). Top-4 positive writers carry only .573 of positive mass, so no small cut reproduces the final cut -- which is why the S1600 completeness prediction failed. Head grain lands on certified question-circuit heads (10.5/9.7/9.3/12.6) from a decomposition that never used the circuit labels.

depth_profile.method: per-component signed contribution summed in stack order; 96 fit rows (skip=80) + 96 held-out (skip=15000); recon rel err 6.3e-08 / 0.0

preds.pred_c_drawdown_ge_25pct_and_replicates: FAILED (fit .249442 misses the .25 bar by .00056; held-out .4687, relative gap .879 vs a .20 bar)

depth_profile.replicates: monotone accumulation with no front/middle reversal; peak at attn16; suppression confined to MLPs (mlp16, mlp17) while attn17 still writes POSITIVELY (+138.7); mlp17 the dominant drop
depth_profile.does_not_replicate: SUPERSEDED by S1603 -- resolved with 6 samples; see spread_resolution.
depth_profile.corrects: S1601's 'mlp11 is the main mid-depth source' framing: mlp11 is the largest single step but accumulation continues five more layers, adding a further ~1245 (31% of peak) after it. The channel is built across the WHOLE stack, not mid-stack.

spread_resolution.samples: 6 disjoint 96-row sets (skip 80/15000/20000/25000/30000/35000), no refitting; recon rel err 0.0-1.5e-07 throughout
spread_resolution.shape: peak = attn16 in 6/6; largest negative step = mlp17 in 6/6
spread_resolution.supersedes: the S1602 'magnitude open' flag: the channel loses .358 +/- .029 of its attn16 peak before the readout
spread_resolution.why_S1602_looked_unstable: S1602's two samples were the MIN (.2494) and the MAX (.4687) of the six; the other four cluster at .3477-.3806 (spread .033). Drawing both extremes from six has p ~ 1/15. S1602's pred_c stays FAILED as written -- .249442 missed a .25 bar by .00056 -- but .2494 was the low outlier, not the quantity.

_slice_writer_graph.standing_statement: S1600-1603: heads 9.7/10.5 + mlp9/mlp10 write '?' evidence into span(v1,v2), which IS the '?' unembedding direction (logit-lens rank 1). The channel accumulates MONOTONICALLY across the whole stack with no front/middle reversal, peaking at attn16 (6/6); mlp11 is the largest single positive step (+1028) but only ~69% of the peak is reached by then. Suppression is MLP-only and late: mlp16 (-292) and mlp17 (-1151, largest of any sign) cut it back by .358 +/- .029 while attn17 still writes positively (+139). The late-peak SHAPE is general (12/12, two classes, two sites) but the READ-WRITE relationship is NOT: mlp11 amplifies the channel it reads (+1028) while mlp17 opposes its own payload (-1374 to -5111), so any 'module X reads and writes the same variable' claim needs testing per site (S1604). No small component set reproduces the final cut (top-4 positive = .414) because the quantity is assembled by ~34 positive steps against 2 large negative ones.

pronouns_depth_profile.slice: pos_r8 payload (8 most POSITIVE eigendirections; S1598 rule -- mlp17 slices must be sign-split, never |lambda|-ordered)
pronouns_depth_profile.samples: 6 disjoint 96-row sets; recon rel err 1.1e-07 to 3.6e-07
pronouns_depth_profile.passed: peak at layer >=14 in 6/6 (attn16 x5, attn17 x1). With question's attn16 6/6 (S1603) the late-peak whole-stack-accumulation shape is 12/12 ACROSS TWO CLASSES AND TWO SITES -- the most robust result in the S1600-1604 arc.
pronouns_depth_profile.failed_pred_b: mlp17 is a large NEGATIVE writer of its OWN payload subspace in 6/6 (-1374 to -5111); predicted top-2 POSITIVE. The S1601 read-write coincidence (mlp11 was the largest positive writer of the subspace it reads) does NOT generalise.
pronouns_depth_profile.failed_pred_c: mean drawdown .5050 vs a registered <= .10. Sign-splitting the READ basis does not remove suppression because the suppression is a WRITE.
pronouns_depth_profile.driver_error: conflated how a form READS with how a module WRITES: the eigen-sign of the class-projected form describes the module as a reader of the residual and carries no information about the sign of its output along those same directions.

do_not_overread.vs_question: pronouns .5050 +/- .1095 vs question .3584 +/- .0287 is 1.30 sigma -- NOT significant. 'Pronouns is suppressed more' is unsupported.
do_not_overread.magnitude_open: pronouns sem .1095 (sd .2682) is well above the .05 that closed question in S1603. Six samples do NOT pin the pronouns drawdown; the SIGN is certain (6/6), the SIZE is not.

pronouns_depth_profile.unregistered_stable: top-2 positive writers are mlp12, mlp13 in 6/6 -- NOT S1598's set (mlp16, x0, mlp15, mlp9, mlp14, attn9), which was measured into the |lambda|-top-8 slice. THE WRITER SET IS A PROPERTY OF THE (site, slice-rule) PAIR, NOT OF THE CLASS ALONE -- a caution for every writer-graph number in this program.
pronouns_depth_profile.in_flight: readwrite_2x2: {question,pronouns} x {mlp11,mlp17} under one uniform slice rule, to identify whether SITE or CLASS decides the read-write sign (S1601 and S1604 differ in both, so neither is identified).

readwrite_2x2.design: {question,pronouns} x {mlp11,mlp17}, one uniform pos_r8 payload rule, 3 disjoint samples per cell; recon rel err 6.3e-08 to 3.6e-07
readwrite_2x2.finding: THE SELF-WRITE SIGN TRACKS THE CLASS, NOT THE SITE. Question writes INTO its payload directions at both sites (6/6 samples); pronouns writes AGAINST its own at both (6/6). The S1601-vs-S1604 contrast previously attributed to depth is a class difference. The driver's site hypothesis was exactly inverted and all three registered bars FAILED.
readwrite_2x2.instrument_limit: TWO OF FOUR CELLS ARE DEGENERATE AND THEIR DEPTH CURVES MUST NOT BE USED: question@mlp17 peaks at layers 1-2 with drawdowns nan/nan/35.85 (curve never rises, ratio divides by ~0); pronouns@mlp11 peaks at the TERMINAL component so drawdown is exactly 0.000 by construction. Both are OFF-SITE cells. The depth-curve method yields a coherent accumulation profile ONLY at a class's own certified site. Self-write is a signed sum with no division and stays valid everywhere, which is why the class-not-site conclusion survives while cross-cell drawdown/peak comparisons do not.
readwrite_2x2.do_not_use: the |mlp17|/|mlp11| ratios (.771 question, 17.11 pronouns) -- question's numerator comes from a degenerate curve

writer_floor_control.finding: A RANDOM rank-8 subspace has 'writers': consensus top-6 mlp17, mlp16, mlp15, attn16, attn17, attn13. Component attribution onto ANY low-rank subspace is dominated by the largest-output-norm components. All three real slice rules at pronouns@mlp17 share exactly {mlp17, mlp16, mlp15} with the random control.
writer_floor_control.floor_corrected: raw Jaccard(|lambda|-rule, payload-rule) = .333; FLOOR-CORRECTED = .000 -- the entire apparent agreement between two slice rules was the floor. Rule-specific tails are disjoint: |lambda| picks x0/attn12/mlp9, payload picks mlp11/mlp12/mlp13, gate picks mlp14/x0/attn12.
writer_floor_control.passed: Jaccard(|lambda|, gate) .714 > Jaccard(|lambda|, payload) .333 -- the |lambda| slice at a suppression-dominated site is gate-dominated (S1598's own lesson, confirmed from the other side).
writer_floor_control.standing_requirement: EVERY component-level writer/attribution claim needs a random-subspace control at matched rank; only the floor-corrected set may be named as writers. LESSONS 15.
